about.does.1: Reads Windows settings and Riot installation files.
about.does.2: Checks that public Riot servers answer (only when you press the button).
about.does.3: Changes Windows settings and Riot Client files — only with your permission, step by step.
about.does.4: Lets you undo every change with one button.
about.does.5: Starts the Riot Client the same way its own shortcut does.
about.doesnt.1: Does not touch the game, its files or its memory.
about.doesnt.2: Does not disable or bypass Vanguard anti-cheat.
about.doesnt.3: Does not ask for or store your login and password.
about.doesnt.4: Does not press keys or click for you in the game or client.
about.doesnt.5: Does not show other players' stats or hidden information.
about.doesnt.6: Does not send any data anywhere. No VPN, proxy or “accelerators”.
about.license: Free and open source (MIT license). No ads, no telemetry, no registration.
about.privacy: Everything stays on this computer. Reports are copied or saved only when you press the button.
about.title: About Netwick
app.webview2_missing:
Netwick needs Microsoft Edge WebView2 to show its window, and it is not installed on this computer.

Open the official Microsoft download page?
bonjour.running: Apple Bonjour (mDNS) is running. Usually harmless, but it sometimes conflicts with the network — it can be stopped for a while.
bonjour.stopped: Bonjour is installed but not running.
check.crashed: This check stopped unexpectedly and was skipped.
check.timeout: This check took too long and was skipped.
check.unknown: Could not check this. It is not necessarily a problem.
conn.wifi: You are on Wi-Fi. A wired connection is more stable for online games.
conn.wired: Connected by cable — the most stable option.
demo.hint: Demo mode: Windows is simulated, nothing on this computer is changed.
demo.switched: Demo: {scenario}. The computer was “reset” to this situation.
disclaimer.ru_note: Netwick is not affiliated with Riot Games. The program does not touch the game or anti-cheat, does not ask for passwords, and works only with Windows settings.
disclaimer.short: Netwick is not affiliated with Riot Games.
disk.low: Only {freeGb} GB free on drive {drive}. Updates need space — free up at least 30 GB.
disk.no_game: Skipped: the game was not found.
drivers.found: Drivers that Riot lists as problematic were found: {files}. This matters only if you see a VAN error about drivers.
drivers.ok: No drivers known to conflict with Vanguard.
error.check_failed: The check could not finish. Please try again.
error.open_system: Could not open this Windows window. Open it from the Start menu instead.
firewall.blocked: Windows Firewall blocks: {apps}. The game cannot connect until this rule is removed.
firewall.no_install: Skipped: the game was not found.
firewall.ok: Windows Firewall does not block the game.
fix.F01.know: Unsaved progress in the client will be lost. Vanguard is not touched.
fix.F01.manual1: Close the game and the Riot Client (right-click the tray icon → Exit).
fix.F01.manual2: Start the Riot Client from the desktop shortcut.
fix.F01.title: Restart the Riot Client
fix.F01.what: Close the Riot Client and the game, then start the Riot Client again the same way its own shortcut does.
fix.F01.why: Riot recommends restarting the Riot Client for many error codes.
fix.F02.know: Takes a second. Nothing else changes.
fix.F02.manual1: Open Start, type “cmd”, right-click Command Prompt → Run as administrator.
fix.F02.title: Clear the DNS cache
fix.F02.what: Ask Windows to forget saved server addresses so it looks them up again.
fix.F02.why: Recommended by Riot support when the client cannot reach its servers.
fix.F03.know: The internet will disconnect for a few seconds.
fix.F03.title: Renew the IP address
fix.F03.what: Ask your router for a fresh network address and clear the DNS cache.
fix.F03.why: Part of Riot's DNS guide for connection problems.
fix.F04.know: We remember your current settings so they can be restored.
fix.F04.manual1: Open Settings → Network & internet → your connection → Hardware properties.
fix.F04.manual2: Next to “DNS server assignment” click Edit → Manual → IPv4 on.
fix.F04.title: Use public DNS 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4
fix.F04.what: Set the DNS servers of your active network connection to 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4 — the addresses from Riot's guide.
fix.F04.why: Riot recommends a public DNS when address lookups fail or are outdated.
fix.F05.know: A restart will be required. If you have a static IP or VPN configured, they will need to be set up again.
fix.F05.manual2: Type netsh int ip reset and press Enter.
fix.F05.manual3: Type netsh winsock reset and press Enter.
fix.F05.manual4: Type netsh winhttp reset proxy and press Enter.
fix.F05.title: Reset Windows network settings
fix.F05.what: Restore Windows network settings (TCP/IP, Winsock and the WinHTTP proxy) to defaults.
fix.F05.why: Recommended by Riot support for connection drops.
fix.F06.know: Only our own rules are added. Your other rules are not touched.
fix.F06.manual1: Open Start → “Allow an app through Windows Firewall”.
fix.F06.manual2: Click Change settings → Allow another app.
fix.F06.title: Allow the game in Windows Firewall
fix.F06.what: Add “allow” rules for VALORANT.exe, vgc.exe and RiotClientServices.exe. Rule names start with “Netwick — ”.
fix.F06.why: Riot's firewall guide (error VAL 29) asks to allow these programs.
fix.F07.know: Riot recommends restarting the PC afterwards.
fix.F07.manual1: Press Win+R, type services.msc and press Enter.
fix.F07.manual3: Set Startup type to Automatic, click OK, restart the PC.
fix.F07.title: Start Vanguard together with Windows
fix.F07.what: Set the Vanguard service (vgc) start type to “Automatic”.
fix.F07.why: Riot recommends this for errors VAN -81, VAN 57, VAN 68 and VAN 128.
fix.F08.know: A restart is required. Only used for VAN 128.
fix.F08.manual2: Under Startup and Recovery click Settings.
fix.F08.manual3: Set “Write debugging information” to (none), click OK, restart.
fix.F08.title: Turn off crash dump writing
fix.F08.why: Riot's article for VAN 128 lists this step.
fix.F09.know: Killer network features (traffic priority) will stop working until you undo this.
fix.F09.manual1: Press Win+R, type services.msc, press Enter.
fix.F09.title: Turn off Killer Network Service
fix.F09.what: Stop Killer Network Service and set it to “Disabled”.
fix.F09.why: For VAN 68 Riot recommends disabling it.
fix.F10.know: Other lines in the file are not touched. A backup copy is made first.
fix.F10.manual3: Delete lines with riotgames.com, riotcdn.net and pvp.net (and NETWICK markers, if any), save.
fix.F10.title: Remove Riot routes from hosts
fix.F10.what: Remove Riot server addresses that Netwick or other tools wrote into the hosts file.
fix.F10.why: Pinned addresses go stale over time and start breaking the connection. Without them the client finds working ones by itself.
fix.F11.know: You stay signed in. The client will rebuild the cache. Vanguard is not touched.
fix.F11.manual1: Close the Riot Client and the game.
fix.F11.manual3: Delete the Cache and Crashpad folders.
fix.F11.title: Clear the Riot Client cache
fix.F11.what: Close the Riot Client and the game and delete the client's temporary files: Cache, Crashpad and crash reports.
fix.F11.why: A damaged cache often stops the client from updating or connecting. This step is not in Riot articles, but it is safe: the client rebuilds the cache.
fix.F12.after: Sign in again when the client starts.
fix.F12.know: You will need to sign in to your Riot account again — have your login ready. Netwick never sees or stores it.
fix.F12.manual4: Start the client and sign in again.
fix.F12.title: Reset the sign-in session
fix.F12.what: Close the client and delete the Riot Client's local session and settings files.
fix.F12.why: Helps with VAL 43 and sign-in hangs when the saved session is broken. This step is not in Riot articles.
fix.F13.know: Better close the game first. If the service is disabled, the “Turn on Vanguard automatic start” step is needed first.
fix.F13.title: Restart the Vanguard service
fix.F13.what: Stop and start the Vanguard service (vgc) again. The vgk driver and settings are not touched.
fix.F13.why: A stuck service is a common cause of VAN errors. A restart often helps without restarting the PC. This step is not in Riot articles.
fix.F14.after: Launch the game so the client picks up the new addresses.
fix.F14.know: A hosts backup is made first. Entries are dated and re-tested: if an address stops working, Netwick offers to remove it.
fix.F14.manual1: Open Repair → Servers and routes and look at the working addresses.
fix.F14.manual2: Open Notepad as administrator and the file C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts.
fix.F14.manual3: Add a line “address server-name”, save, and run ipconfig /flushdns.
fix.F14.title: Pin working server addresses
fix.F14.what: Test Riot server addresses and, where some addresses fail, write the fastest working one into hosts.
fix.F14.why: If your provider or network cuts transfers on some addresses, the client can get stuck on a bad one — one of the causes of VAL 43. This step is not in Riot articles.
fix.F15.know: iTunes and some network printers need Bonjour — it starts again after a restart or with the Undo button.
fix.F15.title: Stop the Bonjour service
fix.F15.what: Stop the Apple Bonjour (mDNS) service. Nothing is uninstalled.
fix.F15.why: Bonjour sometimes conflicts with the Windows network stack. This step is not in Riot articles.
fix.error.adapter: No active network connection was found to change.
fix.error.backup: Could not make a backup, so nothing was changed.
fix.error.declined: You declined the Windows permission request. Nothing was changed.
fix.error.files_locked: Client files are in use. Close the Riot Client and try again.
fix.error.generic: Could not apply this change. Nothing else was touched.
fix.error.hosts_locked: The hosts file is locked, probably by an antivirus. Nothing was changed.
fix.error.invalid_undo: This change record looks damaged and was skipped.
fix.error.no_client: Riot Client was not found. Install it from the official website.
fix.error.no_install: The game was not found, so there is nothing to allow.
fix.error.scenario: This step is only for a specific error code.
fix.error.vgc_disabled: The Vanguard service is disabled. First turn on its automatic start.
fix.error.vgc_missing: Vanguard is not installed. The Riot Client will install it.
fix.error.worker: The helper process did not respond. Nothing was changed.
guide.G01.intro: Removing Vanguard and letting the game install it again fixes many Vanguard errors.
guide.G01.s1: Right-click the Vanguard icon in the tray → Advanced → Uninstall Vanguard. Or open “Add or remove programs” → Riot Vanguard → Uninstall.
guide.G01.s3: Start the game — Vanguard will install itself.
guide.G01.s4: Restart the computer once more when asked.
guide.G01.title: Reinstall Vanguard
guide.G02.intro: Start Windows with only Microsoft services to see if another program gets in the way.
guide.G02.s1: Press Win+R, type msconfig, press Enter.
guide.G02.s2: On the Services tab tick “Hide all Microsoft services”.
guide.G02.s4: Important: tick “vgc” again so Vanguard keeps working.
guide.G02.s5: Open Task Manager → Startup apps and disable the items there. Write down what you disabled.
guide.G02.s6: Restart the PC and test the game. Then turn items back on one by one.
guide.G02.title: Clean Boot
guide.G03.intro: These options live in computer settings (BIOS/UEFI), not in Windows. Netwick cannot change them.
guide.G03.s1: Open “System Information” to see the current state (BIOS mode, Secure Boot state).
guide.G03.s2: Open the official Riot guide below and find your motherboard or laptop maker.
guide.G03.s3: Restart the PC, enter BIOS (usually Del, F2 or F10) and turn on the option as the guide shows.
guide.G03.s4: Save and restart, then run the check again.
guide.G03.title: Turn on TPM 2.0, Secure Boot or IOMMU
guide.G03.warn: If you are unsure — ask someone knowledgeable. Wrong BIOS changes can stop the computer from starting. If BitLocker is on, keep your recovery key ready.
guide.G04.intro: Memory Integrity is a Windows security feature that Riot may require.
guide.G04.s1: Open Windows Security → Device security → Core isolation details.
guide.G04.title: Turn on Memory Integrity
guide.G05.intro: Error VAN 9002 and VAN 128 appear when Windows protections were changed from defaults.
guide.G05.s1: Open Windows Security → App & browser control → Exploit protection settings.
guide.G05.s2: On “System settings” set Control flow guard, DEP, ASLR (all three), SEHOP and Heap integrity to “Use default (On)”.
guide.G05.s3: On “Program settings” remove entries for Riot and VALORANT programs.
guide.G05.title: Restore Windows exploit protection
guide.G05.warn: Change only the settings listed here.
guide.G06.intro: Riot may need a newer Windows version. Updates are installed by Windows itself.
guide.G06.s2: Click “Check for updates” and install everything offered.
guide.G06.s3: Restart the computer, even if Windows does not ask.
guide.G06.title: Update Windows
guide.G07.intro: Some disk and Wi-Fi drivers conflict with Vanguard. Riot's article explains which driver to install for your device.
guide.G07.s1: Open the official Riot article below and find the driver named in your error.
guide.G07.s2: Follow the steps there to update or replace it (via Device Manager or the manufacturer's page linked in the article).
guide.G07.s3: Unplug extra USB devices and restart the computer.
guide.G07.title: Update or replace the driver
guide.G07.warn: Replacing a disk driver incorrectly can stop Windows from starting. If unsure, ask someone knowledgeable.
guide.G08.intro: Riot Support recommends testing without a VPN or proxy.
guide.G08.s1: Close your VPN app or disconnect it (look for its icon near the clock).
guide.G08.s2: Open Settings → Network & internet → Proxy and turn off “Use a proxy server”.
guide.G08.title: Turn off VPN or proxy
guide.G09.intro: Riot's article says Avast and AVG can stop the update at 0%.
guide.G09.s1: Open the official Riot article below.
guide.G09.s2: Temporarily turn on Passive Mode in Avast or AVG following the links in the article.
guide.G09.title: Antivirus blocks the update (stuck at 0%)
guide.G09.warn: Riot notes this is done at your own risk. Turn protection back on right after the update.
guide.G10.intro: Simple steps from Riot's connection guide.
guide.G10.s1: If possible, connect the computer with a cable instead of Wi-Fi.
guide.G10.s2: Restart the router: unplug it, wait at least 30 seconds, plug it back in.
guide.G10.s3: Pause downloads, streams and updates on other devices and apps.
guide.G10.title: Check the network
guide.G11.intro: If nothing else helps, Riot recommends reinstalling the game.
guide.G11.s1: Open “Add or remove programs” and uninstall the game.
guide.G11.s3: Install the game again from the Riot Client.
guide.G11.title: Reinstall the game
guide.G12.intro: This is not a computer error, but a restriction. Fixes will not help.
guide.G12.s1: Read the official Riot article about hardware bans below.
guide.G12.s2: If you believe it is a mistake, submit a ticket to Riot Support.
guide.G12.title: Hardware restriction
guide.G13.intro: If nothing helped, Riot Support can look at your logs.
guide.G13.s1: Gather logs with the official Riot Repair Tool (link below).
guide.G13.s2: Copy the Netwick report (Report for support).
guide.G13.s3: Submit a ticket on the Riot Support website and attach both.
guide.G13.title: Contact Riot Support
guide.G14.intro: A firewall rule blocks the game. Blocking rules win over allow rules, so it must be removed by hand.
guide.G14.s1: Open “Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security”.
guide.G14.s2: Open Inbound Rules and Outbound Rules.
guide.G14.s3: Find rules with a red “block” sign for VALORANT, vgc or Riot Client.
guide.G14.title: Remove the blocking firewall rule
guide.G15.intro: This is not an error, but on laptops and in power-saving modes the game can lose frames and responsiveness. Netwick changes nothing — the settings are yours.
guide.G15.s1: Plug the laptop into the charger.
guide.G15.s2: In the Power window pick “Balanced” or “Best performance”.
guide.G15.s3: In the Game Mode window turn the switch on.
guide.G15.title: Power and Game Mode
help.safe: Netwick relies on Riot and Microsoft articles; steps that are not in them are marked. It never touches the game or the anti-cheat.
help.step.1: Press “Check computer”. Netwick only reads settings — it takes about 10 seconds.
help.step.2: Read the result: green — all good, yellow — can be improved, red — found the cause.
help.step.3: Press “Fix”. Each step explains what will change, and asks before doing anything.
help.step.4: If something went wrong, press “Undo Netwick changes” at the top.
help.step.5: Need more control? Open “Repair”: every scenario is there separately, including the server node check and routes.
help.title: How Netwick works
hogs.found: These apps may be using the internet: {apps}. Pause their downloads while playing.
hogs.none: No apps that usually download a lot are running.
home.check_hint: Only reads settings. Nothing is changed without your permission.
home.code_label: I have an error with a code
home.subtitle: Netwick checks your computer in about 10 seconds and explains what to do.
home.title: Something wrong with the game?
hosts.clean: No old entries from previous tools.
hosts.legacy: Found {count} old hosts entries that send the client to fixed addresses. They go stale — we recommend removing them.
hosts.managed: Netwick has pinned working addresses in hosts ({count}). They are re-tested on every check.
info.check_email.text: The account may be restricted. Check the e-mail linked to your account for messages from Riot.
info.check_email.title: Check your e-mail
info.delete_sys.text: Riot's article explains how to delete the driver file by hand if needed. Netwick never deletes driver files — follow the article carefully.
info.delete_sys.title: If the file is still there
info.practice_range.text: Start a Practice Range or a custom game to see whether the error appears outside of matchmaking.
info.practice_range.title: Test in the Range
info.reboot.after: After the restart, open Netwick again and run the check.
info.reboot.text: Riot recommends a full restart first: it clears many temporary problems. Save your work, restart, then come back.
info.reboot.title: Restart the computer
info.riot_id.text: Your name is not allowed. Change your Riot ID on the official Riot account page.
info.riot_id.title: Change your Riot ID
info.server_status.text: Open the official Riot status page to see if there is an outage or maintenance.
info.server_status.title: Check Riot server status
info.sign_out_other.text: Make sure your account is not signed in on another computer, then restart the client.
info.sign_out_other.title: Sign out on other devices
info.time_sync.text: Open Settings → Time & language → Date & time, turn on “Set time automatically” and click “Sync now”.
info.time_sync.title: Set the clock automatically
info.uninstall_driver_software.text: The error names a driver file. Find the program that installed it in “Add or remove programs”, uninstall it and restart.
info.uninstall_driver_software.title: Uninstall the program named in the error
info.usb.text: Leave only the keyboard and mouse. Unplug controllers, hubs, card readers and similar devices, then try again.
info.usb.title: Unplug extra USB devices
info.wait.text: If there is maintenance or an outage, nothing on your computer needs fixing — wait and try again.
info.wait.title: Try again later
install.no_game: Riot Client is installed, but the game was not found. Install the game from the Riot Client.
install.not_found: Game not found. Install the Riot Client and the game from the official website.
install.ok: Riot Client and the game are installed. Game folder: {game}
iommu.off: Kernel DMA protection (IOMMU) is off. Usually this is fine, but Riot may ask some players to turn it on.
iommu.unknown: Could not check kernel DMA protection. You can see it in “System Information” (msinfo32).
killer.found: Killer Network Service is installed. For error VAN 68 Riot recommends turning it off.
killer.none: Killer Network Service is not installed or already off.
logs.clean: No connection errors in recent Riot Client sessions.
logs.core_errors: The Riot Client recently had connection errors with important servers: {hosts}.
logs.extra_errors: The Riot Client had errors with secondary servers ({hosts}). If the game works — no action needed.
logs.recovered: No connection errors in the last client session (there were earlier).

medal.first_check.name: First check

medal.safe_hands.name: Safety net
medal.scout.name: Scout

medal.streak3.text: Checks three days in a row

nav.label: Main menu
nodes.how_1: A route is a line in the hosts file that sends the client to one specific working address. A backup is made before writing.
nodes.how_2: Entries are dated and re-tested on every check. If an address stops working, Netwick offers to remove it.
nodes.how_3: This method is not in Riot articles. The client usually switches to a working address by itself — pin only if errors keep coming back.
nodes.state.mixed: {good} of {total} work — a working one exists
nodes.subtitle: Every address is tested for real: connection, secure channel and the full response. That shows when a connection opens but data gets cut off.
nodes.title: Servers and routes
nodes.verdict.all_down: No Riot server passed the test. Check the internet, VPN and antivirus. If the game works anyway, the test was wrong.
nodes.verdict.needed: {count} servers have some addresses that do not work. The client may land on a bad one — you can pin a working one.
nodes.verdict.ok: All tested Riot servers work. Nothing needs pinning.
nodes.verdict.some_down: Some servers do not answer at all. A route won't help — there is nothing to switch to.
ondemand.blocked: To keep On-Demand mode working we will not change the Vanguard start type. Riot's official steps for On-Demand:
ondemand.not_ready: On-Demand mode (protection only while playing) is not available yet. Missing: {missingText}.
ondemand.question.text: Did you turn on the mode where Vanguard protection runs only while you play (On-Demand)?
ondemand.question.title: One question before we continue
ondemand.ready: Your PC meets the requirements for On-Demand mode: protection will only run while playing. This is an official Riot feature.
ondemand.steps.2: If the error stays, reinstall Vanguard (uninstall, restart, start the game).
ondemand.steps.3: Check On-Demand readiness with the official Vanguard Pre-Check.
power.issue.battery: The laptop is on battery — plug in the charger.
power.issue.saver: The “Power saver” plan is on — the processor runs slower.
power.issues: Windows may slow the game down: some power settings are worth adjusting.
power.ok: Power plan and Game Mode are fine for gaming.
profile.card_empty: Run your first check — your PC's health score will appear here.
profile.empty_text: Run your first full check — a health score and medals will appear here.
profile.open_text: Health score, check history and medals.
profile.privacy: The data never leaves this computer. File: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Netwick\profile.json
profile.reset_text: The check history, counters and medals will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
profile.subtitle: Everything is stored only on this computer. Every full check adds a point to the history.
profile.title: Your PC's game health
progress.cancelled_note: The check was stopped early, so some results are missing.
progress.label: Check progress
progress.subtitle: This takes about 10 seconds. Nothing is changed.
progress.title: Checking your computer…
proxyvpn.both: A VPN and a proxy are turned on. Riot Support recommends temporarily turning them off for testing.
proxyvpn.proxy: A proxy is turned on in Windows. Riot Support recommends temporarily turning it off for testing.
proxyvpn.vpn: A VPN is turned on ({adapters}). Riot Support recommends temporarily turning it off for testing.
quality.grade.bad: The connection is unstable — expect lag and disconnects.
quality.tip.fine: If the game still lags, the problem is probably not your connection to Riot servers.
quality.tip.loss: There is packet loss: restart the router (unplug for 30 seconds) and pause downloads.
quality.tip.run_fix: Open Repair → Servers and routes: it shows which server addresses do not answer.
quality.tip.wifi: Looks like Wi-Fi trouble: use a cable or move closer to the router.
reboot.cancel_failed: Could not cancel. Run in Command Prompt: shutdown /a
reboot.failed: Could not schedule a restart. Restart the computer manually.
reboot.maybe: Some programs are waiting for a restart. If something does not work, restart the PC.
reboot.ok: Windows is not waiting for a restart.
reboot.pending: Windows is waiting for a restart after updates — restart your PC, this often helps.
reboot.scheduled: The computer will restart in 60 seconds. Save your work. After the restart, open Netwick and run the check.
repair.note: Steps without a Riot article link are marked in the wizard. Everything reversible can be undone with the button at the top.
repair.subtitle: Every scenario on its own. Before starting we list the steps — untick what you don't want. Every change asks first.
repair.title: Repair and maintenance
report.privacy: Personal data was removed from this report automatically.
report.rrt_hint: For a Riot ticket, also gather logs with the official Riot Repair Tool.
report.subtitle: Only Netwick check results. No logs, passwords, account names, user name, computer name or home IP.
report.title: Report for support
result.not_found_text: We did not find the cause on your computer. Look up your error code, or contact Riot Support.
result.unknown: {count} checks could not run. This does not mean something is wrong.
riotstatus.incident: Riot reports an outage: “{title_en}”. Most likely the problem is not on your side — better wait.
riotstatus.ok: Riot reports no outages or maintenance (region: {region}).
riotstatus.unreachable: Could not get the Riot server status.

scenario.bonjour.title: Bonjour service

scenario.nodes.title: Servers and routes

scenario.quick.title: Quick repair
scenario.routes_reset.text: Remove all Riot addresses that Netwick or other tools wrote into hosts.
scenario.routes_reset.title: Remove routes
scenario.support.text: What to prepare and where to write if nothing helped.
scenario.support.title: Riot Support
scenario.undo.title: Undo everything

scenario.vanguard.title: Reinstall Vanguard
search.caveat: Riot warns that error codes are sometimes displayed incorrectly.
search.examples: You can type it any way: 68, van68, VAN-81, val 43, VAN: RESTRICTION: 3.

search.title: Find an error by code
search.verified: Checked against the official article on {date}.
secureboot.off_win10: Secure Boot is off. Windows 10 does not require it, but some players may be asked to turn it on.
secureboot.off_win11: Secure Boot is off. Windows 11 needs it for game protection. It is turned on in computer settings (BIOS) — we will show you how.
servers.all_down: Computer cannot communicate with Riot servers. Let's check the internet connection.
servers.cert_issue: Some secure connections were not trusted ({hosts}). Usually this is caused by a wrong clock or antivirus HTTPS scanning.
servers.client_errors: The Riot Client had connection errors with: {hosts}.
servers.extra_down: These are not core game servers ({hosts}). If the game launches — this can be safely ignored.
servers.mixed: Some server addresses do not respond ({hosts}). The client usually switches by itself, but if errors repeat you can pin a working address.
servers.pinned_dead: An old entry in the hosts file sends the game to an address that no longer works: {hosts}.
servers.some_down: Some important Riot servers do not respond: {hosts}.
settings.clear_history_hint: The check history is stored only on this computer.
settings.title: Settings
settings.tray_hint: Quick access: Check, Ready to play?, Open.
settings.update_hint: Only shows that a new version is out with a link. Nothing is downloaded.
settings.watch: Check when the Riot Client starts
settings.watch_hint: Netwick looks at the process list every 5 seconds and shows a message only if it finds a problem. It never interacts with the client.
specs.arm: This computer has an ARM processor ({arch}). The game supports only regular x64 processors.
specs.cpu: The processor does not support the instructions the game needs (SSE 4.2 or AVX).
specs.ok: The computer meets the minimum requirements ({ramGb} GB of memory).
specs.ram: Only {gb} GB of memory. The game needs at least 4 GB.
specs.vm: Windows is running inside a virtual machine. The game does not work in virtual machines.
support.before_text: Auto-repair goes through all safe steps in order. Code search shows steps for your error.
support.privacy: Netwick sends nothing by itself — the report reaches support only if you paste it.
support.s1.text: If Riot has an outage or maintenance, there is no need to write — just wait.
support.s1.title: Check server status
support.s2.text: The report has check results and what was already done. User name, PC name and IP addresses are removed automatically.
support.s2.title: Copy the Netwick report
support.s3.text: Riot's official tool collects client logs for support. Download it from the link and follow the article.
support.s3.title: Collect logs with Riot Repair Tool
support.s4.text: Give the error code, when it appears and what you already tried. Paste the Netwick report and attach the log archive.
support.s4.title: Submit a ticket
support.subtitle: If the steps did not help, Riot Support can look deeper. The more you attach, the faster the answer.
support.title: Contact Riot Support
time.no_reference: Could not compare the clock: Riot servers did not answer.
time.wrong: The clock is off by about {offset} seconds. A wrong time breaks the connection and Vanguard protection.
tip.1: Close torrents and cloud uploads before playing: they eat bandwidth and raise your ping.
tip.10: Run a check after big Windows updates — problems show up before you launch the game.
tip.11: Do not trust tools that promise to “boost ping”: there are no safe miracles.
tip.12: Netwick keeps history only on your computer — you can erase it in settings.
tip.2: A cable beats Wi-Fi: lower and steadier ping.
tip.3: If your router runs for months, unplug it for 30 seconds every couple of weeks.
tip.4: Restart your PC when Windows asks: pending updates often break the protection.
tip.5: Keep free space on the game drive: updates need at least 30 GB.
tip.6: Look up error codes in Netwick: steps come in the order Riot recommends.
tip.7: Close the game and save your work before bigger network changes — some steps need a restart.
tip.8: VPN and proxy sometimes break signing in: turn them off while testing.
tip.9: On a laptop plug in the charger and use a high-performance plan before a match.
tip.label: Tip of the day
tools.conn.latency: average connection time to Riot servers
tools.conn.text: Checks the connection type, apps using the internet and average delay to Riot servers.
tools.conn.tip_none: No obvious problems with the connection.
tools.conn.tip_wifi: A wired connection is more stable than Wi-Fi.
tools.conn.title: Connection advisor
tools.cross.copied: Code copied. Import it in the game settings.
tools.cross.invalid: Enter a name and a valid code.
tools.cross.name: Name
tools.cross.text: Paste a crosshair code exported in the game settings and give it a name. Stored only on this computer.
tools.cross.title: Crosshair notepad
tools.links.demo: In demo mode links open in your browser too.
tools.links.title: Official Riot links
tools.ondemand.note: Netwick only checks. It does not turn On-Demand on. By default Vanguard still starts with Windows.
tools.ondemand.text: On-Demand is an official Riot mode: protection runs only while you play. Your PC needs all of these:
tools.ondemand.title: Vanguard On-Demand readiness
tools.quality.failed: The measurement failed. Check your internet and try again.
tools.quality.no_address: Could not find the server address — looks like there is no internet.
tools.quality.text: We open a connection to a Riot server 12 times in a row: delay, variation (jitter) and loss. Nothing is sent, the game is not contacted — only connections are opened and closed.
tools.quality.title: Connection quality to Riot servers
tools.ready.red: Something is in the way. Run the full check.
tools.ready.text: A quick check of time, Vanguard, Riot servers, VPN, connection and pending restart.
tools.ready.title: Ready to play?
tools.ready.yellow: You can play, but something can be improved.
tools.sens.note: Conversion coefficients are approximate, according to community data.
tools.sens.title: Sensitivity calculator
tools.title: Tools
tpm.off_win10: Security module (TPM 2.0) is off. Windows 10 does not require it, but some players may be asked to turn it on.
tpm.off_win11: Security module (TPM 2.0) is turned off on your computer. Without it, Windows 11 does not allow game protection to run. It is turned on in computer settings (BIOS) — we will show you how.
undo.nothing: Netwick has not changed anything yet — nothing to undo.
undo.partial: Undone: {count}. Some changes could not be undone.
undo.text: Netwick will return these settings to how they were:
undo.title: Undo Netwick changes?
vanguard.normal_off: Vanguard protection is currently off — this is normal, it will turn on with the game.
vanguard.not_installed: Vanguard protection is not installed yet. The Riot Client will install it automatically.
vanguard.vgc_disabled: Windows is preventing Vanguard protection from starting: its service is disabled.
vanguard.vgk_disabled: Windows is preventing the Vanguard driver from starting.
vanguard.vgk_missing: Part of Vanguard protection is missing. Reinstalling Vanguard usually helps.
vbs.off: Memory Integrity is off. Usually this is fine, but Riot may ask some players to turn it on.
vbs.ok: Memory Integrity and virtualization-based security are on.
verdict.green: Computer is ready to play. Riot servers are reachable.
verdict.green_no_servers: No problems found on your computer, but we could not check Riot servers.
verdict.red: We found what is getting in the way.
windows.restriction_hint: Riot may ask for a newer Windows (build 19045 or later) for some players.
windows.unsupported: This Windows version (build {build}) is too old for the game. Windows needs to be updated.
wizard.already: Nothing to change — it was already set up correctly.
wizard.article_text: The official Riot article has the full list of steps for this error.
wizard.check_problem: Something needs attention — the next steps will help.
wizard.end_helped_text: You can launch the game now.
wizard.end_nothing_text: Nothing from the official articles helped. Riot Support can look deeper — we will show how to contact them.
wizard.guide_note: Netwick changes nothing here — these are steps for you.
wizard.helped: Did it help? Try the game.
wizard.plan_text: Steps go from simple to serious. Untick anything you don't want. We still ask before every change.
wizard.reboot_now: Restart the computer for the change to take effect.
wizard.recheck.red: Check again: a problem is still there.
wizard.recheck.unknown: Check again: not everything could be checked.
wizard.recheck.yellow: Check again: some things can still be improved.
wizard.routes.pick_text: Some addresses of these servers do not work. Choose which to pin:
wizard.show_me: Show me how to do it myself
wizard.source_v1: This step is not described in Riot articles.
wizard.undo_yes: Yes — with the “Undo Netwick changes” button at the top.
wizard.waiting_uac: Windows will now ask for permission. Click “Yes” in the window that appears.
